title: Adjacency-preserving bijection characterises graph isomorphism
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and $H$ a simple graph on a vertex set $W$. Then $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic if and only if there is a bijection $\theta \colon V \to W$ such that for all vertices $u, v \in V$, the pair $u, v$ is adjacent in $G$ if and only if $\theta(u), \theta(v)$ is adjacent in $H$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a simple graph on a finite vertex set V
H is a simple graph on a vertex set W
replaced:
\emph{Two simple graphs \texttt{G} and \texttt{H} are isomorphic if and only
if there is a bijection \texttt{$\theta$ : V(G) $\to$ V(H)} such that \texttt{uv $\in$
E(G)} if and only if
\texttt{$\theta$(u)$\theta$(v) $\in$ E(H)}.}
